podcast.title: New Type of Progressive Rock in the 2010s
podcast.body: Djent was identified as a "new type of progressive rock" that rose to prominence in the 2010s. This genre, characterized by its complex and technically demanding nature, contributed to the broader comeback of progressive rock during the decade. "The 2010s saw the rise of a new type of progressive rock called DeGente, which we discussed on a previous episode."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

podcast.title: Progressive Metal Style with Palm-Muting
podcast.body: Djent is a new style of progressive metal, originating in the 2010s, whose name derives from the distinctive sound created when guitarists mute their strings with the palm of their hand. "It emerged as a new style of progressive metal, and the name comes from how guitars mute the strings with the palm of their hand to make a specific sound, like... Digent."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 3: The New Genres
